1. Whether reporters of local newspapers be allowed to see the judgment?

2.       To be referred to the Reporter or not?

 

JUSTICE J.D. KAPOOR, PRESIDENT (ORAL)   Vide impugned order dated 19-01-2001 the appellant has been directed to pay to the respondent the principal amount alongwith interest at the agreed rate minus the amount already paid to the respondent from effective date till maturity and to pay interest for delayed period i.e. from the next day of date of maturity till realization at the agreed rate of interest per annum and Rs. 500/- as legal cost.

2. The impugned order was passed on 19th January, 2001. The appeal has been filed in the year 2006. Explanation of the counsel for the appellant is that appeal could not be filed because proceedings u/s 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act were initiated by the respondent and remained pending for five years. Proceedings u/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act are quasi judicial nature and are for penalty, punishment and sentence for the offence whereas provisions of Consumer Protection Act provides for awarding compensation or refund of disputed amount to a consumer due to deficiency in service or unfair trade practice or sale of defective goods. Both these proceedings are independent of each other. However, misconception of the respondent about the proceedings u/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act vis--vis proceedings under Consumer Protection Act is sufficient ground to condone the delay.

3. Since the matter can be decided without issuing notice to the respondent in just and proper manner on the pleadings of the parties and the rival contentions made before the District Forum and that too without affecting the merits of the case and without substantial variance or modification of the impugned order, the same is being decided at the outset.

4. Admittedly respondent made deposit of Rs. 2 lacs with the appellant by way of FDRs vide cheques No. 47191 dated 23-07-1994 drawn on Canara Bank, East of Kailash, New Delhi for a period of three years and appellant issued post dated cheques No. 74632 to 74639 dated 26-07-1997 amounting to Rs. 4,04,856/- towards principal amount and interest. Respondent made a request for pre-matured refund in the year 1996. On her request two cheques, one bearing No. 149480 dated 31-12-1998 for Rs. 1,40,000/- and another cheque bearing No. 149484 dated 21-12-1998 for Rs. 3,500/- towards full and final settlement.

5. Counsel for the appellant has not been able to produce any term of contract between the parties as to what rate of interest the consumer would be entitled if she asked for pre-mature refund. In such an eventuality the consumer is entitled for agreed rate of interest for the period upto the date of pre-mature refund. Admittedly the payment of pre-mature amount was asked for in the year 1996 but the payments were made in December, 1998. As such the respondent was entitled for agreed rate of interest for the period upto 31-12-1998 i.e. the date of refund of the amount of Rs. 1,43,500/- and a reasonable rate of interest for extra amount she was entitled to.

6. In the result we modify the impugned order in the following terms:-

the appellant shall pay interest at the agreed rate of interest on the deposited amount upto 31st December, 1998 and on the amount exceeding Rs. 1,43,500/- shall pay 9% interest w.e.f. 01-01-1999 till the date of this order

7. Appeal is disposed of in aforesaid terms.

8. F.D.R./Bank Guarantee, if any, furnished by the appellant be returned forthwith after completion of due formalities.

9. A copy of this order as per the statutory requirements, be forwarded to the parties free of charge and also to the concerned District Forum and thereafter the file be consigned to Record Room.

10. Announced on 6th September, 2006.
